texts.facts: 3. The brief facts of the present case are that on 26.06.1999, the food officials consisting of Food Inspectors Sh. Jeet Ram and Sh Gian Chand under the supervision of Local Health Authority/SDM Sh. R.P. Meena reached at Khajuri Khas, Wazirabad Road, where they CA no. 8738/16 Sukhpal Singh & Anrs Vs. Delhi Admn /Food Inspector (PFA) Pages 2 of 15 found a tanker bearing No. HR 38-C-2878 has stored the food article i.e. 'standardized Milk' in its tanker for sale purpose for the use of human consumption ; accused no. 1 Sh. Balraj (since Proclaimed Offender) was the driver of the said tanker and it was found that the milk was being carried for sale in Delhi ; the sample of milk was then lifted as per procedure prescribed under the PFA Act and Rules ; each sample was separately packed, fastened, marked, sealed and necessary documents were prepared at the spot including the Notice as per Form-VI, panchnama etc in the presence of appellant/ accused ; that the price of the sample was paid to the vendor who disclosed that the milk belongs to accused no.2 company i.e. M/s Gopaljee G.K. Dairy & Milk Product (P) Ltd., a partnership Company ; that thereafter one counterpart of sample was sent to Public Analyst (PA) in intact condition and other two counterparts were deposited with SDM/LHA ; - that vide report dated 12.07.1999, PA found the sample to be not conforming to the standards because 'milk solids not fat', it was found to be having 7.02% which was less than the prescribed minimum limit of 8.5% ; - that upon receipt of report, the SDM/LHA ordered investigation which was carried out by Food Inspector and it was revealed that the milk in the tanker belonged to the appellant no2/accused no 2, Company, having two Directors namely Sh Pyare Mohan Dixit and Sh. Radhey Shyam Dixit, and the said company had appointed the appellant no.1 /accused no.3 Mr. Sukhpal Singh, as its Nominee under section 17 PF Act, and as such he was deemed to be in CA no. 8738/16 Sukhpal Singh & Anrs Vs. Delhi Admn /Food Inspector (PFA) Pages 3 of 15 charge of and responsible for the affair of business of their above mentioned company ; that after completion of investigation sanction under Section 20 of the PFA Act was obtained from the Director PFA. The complaint was then filed in the court on 31.01.2000 against all the three accused persons in the capacity of vendor, company and nominee respectively, alleging violation of Section 2(ia)(a), and (m) of PFA Act, as punishable under Section 7/16(1)(a) of PFA. Act. 4. That the complaint was filed in writing by a public servant, hence, recording of pre-summoning evidence was dispensed with and the accused persons were summoned by the learned trial court vide order dated 31.01.2000 for 19.07.2000 to face trial. The presence of accused no.1/driver could Sukhpal Singh vs The State on 7 January, 2021 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/184636406/ 2 not be secured for a very long time, process u/s 82/83 Cr.P.C was issued against him and he was declared proclaimed offenders vide order dated 05.07.2005. The remaining appellant/accused persons appeared to face trial. After filing appearance appellant no. 1/accused no. 3 also represented appellant no. 2/accused no. 2, and filed an application under Section 13(2) of the PFA Act, thereby exercising their right to get the second counterpart of the sample analyzed from the Central Food Laboratory (CFL). The application was allowed and the counter part was sent to the CFL ; director CFL examined the sample and gave his report vide certificate dated 14.06.2000 opining the sample to be adulterated because 'milk fat' was found to be 3.4% which was less than the prescribed minimum limit of 4.5% and also observed 'milk solids not fat' it was found to be 6.4% which was also less than the prescribed minimum limit of 8.5%. CA no. 8738/16 Sukhpal Singh & Anrs Vs. Delhi Admn /Food Inspector (PFA) Pages 4 of 15 5. Thereafter on 21.10.2009 charge was framed against the appellants/accused No.2 and No. 3 being nominee and company for commission of offences punishable u/s 7/16(1)(a) PFA Act for violation of Section 2(ia)(a) and (m) of PFA Act alleging therein that on 26.06.1999 at about 03.15a.m. Balraj s/o Sh. Baldev Raj ( Since Proclaimed Offender ), Vendor cum Driver of Van no. HR 38 C2878 of M/s Gopaljee G.K. Dairy & Milk Product (P) Ltd ( appellant no. 2/accused No. 3) and Sh.Sukhpal Singh,( appellant no. 1/accused no. 3), Quality Control Manager of appellant no. 2/accused No. 2 sold for analysis sample of Standardized Milk,(750 ml), meant for sale for human consumption, ready to sale, after taking it from the above mentioned tanker to Food Inspector Sh. Jeet Ram in the presence of LHA and witnesses of department and on examination of commodity it was analyzed by the Public Analyst of CFL vide Certificate No. G.14-4/2000( PT.1)-273 on 14.06.2000 that the sample is adulterated, it does not conform to standard because 'milk fat' was found to be 3.4% which was less than the prescribed minimum limit of 4.5% and also observed 'milk solids not fat' it was found to be 6.4% which was also less than the prescribed minimum limit of 8.5%. and thereby they all violated the provisions of sub- clause (a) and (m) of Section 2(ia) of PFA Act, 1954 punishable under section 16(1)(a) of PFA Act, 1954 read with Section 7 of the PFA Act to which he pleaded not guilty and claimed trial. 6.1 During trial after the examination and detailed cross examination of three witnesses of the prosecution namely PW1 Sh. Jeet Ram and PW2 Sh. Gian Chand, Food Inspectors,and PW3 Sh. CA no. 8738/16 Sukhpal Singh & Anrs Vs. Delhi Admn /Food Inspector (PFA) Pages 5 of 15 R.P. Meena, the then SDM/LHA now posted as Addl. Commissioner Transport Department, GNCT ofDelhi , prosecution evidence was closed and matter was fixed for Statement of accused . 7. The statement of accused persons were recorded under section 313 Cr.PC in which accused persons pleaded their innocence and stated that Company has no knowledge about the raid conducted by the PFA department on the alleged date of incident ; expressed ignorance about the proceedings dated 26.06.1999 on the ground that no one from the company was present at the spot at that time ; Public Analyst and CFL reports are wrong and unreliable asserting that the complaint had been filed at a belated stage and their right under Section 13(2) of PFA Act stood frustrated ; the Sukhpal Singh vs The State on 7 January, 2021 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/184636406/ 3 shelf like of milk and milk products after adding formalin would be four months and as the present complaint was filed after six months, the product could not be correctly analyzed by the concerned officials. They expressed their intention not to lead defence evidence. Delhi Admn /Food Inspector (PFA) Pages 6 of 15 adulterated food for the use of human consumption through accused no.1 Balraj @ Baldev Raj ( Since Proclaimed Offender) in violation of Section 2(ia)(a) and (m) of PFA Act and has committed the offence punishable u/s 7/16(1A) PFA Act Benefit of section 428 Cr.P.C was also given to the appellant no.1/convict no. 3. 9.(I) The appellant has assailed the judgment and order on sentence passed by the learned trial court by urging various grounds. II) Alternatively, on the quantum of sentence, relying upon the new legislation, it was pleaded that the case of the appellant be considered sympathetically in the light of the preposition of law laid down by the Hon'ble Courts pursuant to coming of new legislation that is Food Safety & Standards Act. 1. For the reasons stated in the application, 90 days' delay in filing the appeal is condoned. In default to undergo SI for 15 days. 2. The respondent/accused has not challenged his conviction or the order on sentence.
texts.arguments: Learned counsel for the Delhi Admn./Food Department, objected to the same and submitted that according to the affidavit of appellants, prosecution has established its case and they be sentenced Sukhpal Singh vs The State on 7 January, 2021 Indian Now Coming to the alternate plea of giving benefit of new legislation to the appellant/ accused. 14. It is argued by learned counsel for the appellant that on the date of pronouncement of judgment/order on sentence, the PFA Act, 1954 was repealed and new act had come into operation. It is stated that the court should give benefit of the new legislation to the accused vide which the punishment provided under the old act has been diluted to a considerable extent, and that the offence for which the accused/appellant has been convicted now falls under the category of Substandard Food punishable under section 51 of the new Act i.e Food and Safety Standards Act, 2006 (hereinafter called FSSAI) punishable with fine of Rs. 5 lacs only. 15. It was argued by learned counsel for the appellant/convicts that appellant no.2 is a Company and appellant no. 1 is a man of old age, respectable person of society, has deep roots in the society, is not working for any gain due to his old age and different types of ailments, has to perform his social and family duties, not involved in any other case and prayed that a lenient view be taken against him in the light of the provisions of law under the new Act. 15.1 Further, that the case pertains to the year 2000, the appellant/accused persons have faced the trial of almost 20 years which by itself is a sufficient punishment ; and the hardship faced by convicts during the said period has caused great mental agony and stress. It is also stated that now a days special circumstances exists due to outbreak of pandemic of Covid-19 and there are chances of CA no. 8738/16 Sukhpal Singh & Anrs Vs. Delhi Admn /Food Inspector (PFA) Pages 9 of 15 appellant no.1. being infected with virus in case imprisonment of sentence is awarded to him and considering the submissions, the fine already imposed by the learned trial court accordingly be reduced. 15.2 In support of his submissions qua the benefit of new legislation, learned counsel for appellant had relied upon the judgment of Nemi Chand Vs. State of Rajasthan ( Crl. Appeals No. 214 and 215 of 2016, vide order dated 10.03.2016, as corrected vide order dated 17.03.2016, as reported in 2016 (1) FAC 203 ) of Hon'ble Supreme Court and earlier judgment T Barai Vs. Henry 1983 ( ) SCC 177. 15.3 Per contra, learned SPP, strongly opposed the submissions advanced by learned counsel by addressing that the sentencing cannot be done in new Act since the definition of many offences are Sukhpal Singh vs The State on 7 January, 2021 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/184636406/ 5 changed in the new Act including this particular offence of which accused is charged. Definition of major offences like "adulteration" and "misbranding" have been changed. Now FSSAI have definition "substandard food", "food containing extraneous matter" "unsafe food" and misbranded food". 15.8 The application of Nemi Chand Judgment (supra), the CA no. 8738/16 Sukhpal Singh & Anrs Vs. Delhi Admn /Food Inspector (PFA) Pages 11 of 15 same is based on the old judgment i.e. T Barai ( Supra) of Hon'ble Supreme Court. The relevant portion of the T Barai Judgment is as follows : - (Para 25) It is settled both on authority and principle that when a later statute again describes an offence created by an earlier statute and imposes a different punishment or varies the procedure, the earlier statute is repealed by implication in Michell Vs. Brown ( 1958) 120 ER 909, 912 : 32 LTOS 146:7 WR 80 Lord Campbell put the matter thus : Sukhpal Singh vs The State on 7 January, 2021 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/184636406/ 6 - "It is well settled rule of construction that, if a later statute again describes an offence created by a former statute and affixes a different punishment, varying the procedure, the earlier statute is repealed by the later statute see also Smith Vs. Benabo ( 1937) 1 ALL ER 523 : ( 1997) 1 KB 518: 156 LT 194" - In Regina Vs. Youle ( 1861) 158 ER 311,315-16 : LT 299 : 9 WR 637 Martin B. said in the oft-quoted passage : - If a statute deals with a particular class of offences, and a subsequent Act is passed which deals with precisely the same offence, and a different punishment is imposed by the later Act, I think that, in effect, the legislature has declared that the new Act shall be substituted for the earlier Act." - The rule is however subject to the limitation contained in Article 20(1) against ex post facto law providing for a greater punishment and has also no application where the offence described in the later Act is not the same as in the earlier Act i.e. when the essential ingredients of the two offences are different. CA no. 8738/16 Sukhpal Singh & Anrs Vs. Delhi Admn /Food Inspector (PFA) Pages 12 of 15 - Moreover, this particular aspect is stated as a illustration in the same judgment in Para 23 which is as follows : - Moreover, this particular aspect is stated as a illustration in the same judgment in Para 23 which is as follows : - To illustrate, if Parliament were to reenact Section 302 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 and provide that the punishment for an offence of murder shall be sentence for imprisonment for life instead of the present sentence of death or imprisonment for life , then it can not be that the courts would still award a sentence of death even in pending cases. Vide said letter the said authority, in the light of judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court in Nemi Chand's Case (supra) issued an advisory to the Commissioners of Food Safety/Officers incharge of Food Safety to dispose of the long pending court cases filed under old PFA Act mainly concerning substandard and misbranding by imposing fine only. B. Because the order of Ld. Appellate Court is against the judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court in Criminal Appeal No.1570/2010 titled as Mithlesh Vs. State of NCT of Delhi wherein it was held that "no further benevolence can be shown to the appellant, more so, when it is a case of food adulteration. E. Because the Ld.Appellate Court did not appreciate the legal position correctly. Sukhpal Singh vs The State on 7 January, 2021 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/184636406/ 10 F. That the petitioner craves leave to this Hon'ble Court to add, amend or drop any of the grounds. G. That no such similar or other petition has been filed either before this Hon'ble Court or before the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India." 3. Learned APP for the State submitted that in decision reported as Mithlesh vs. State of NCT of Delhi (2014) 123 SCC 423, the Apex Court refused to further reduce the sentence observing that it was a case of food adulteration and there was no special circumstance warranting reducing the sentence below the minimum, especially when the High Court had already shown benevolence by reducing the sentence from one year to three months. 4. Mr.K.K.Manan, Learned Senior Counsel appearing on behalf of the respondent has submitted that the case of the respondent is squarely covered by this recent decision of the Supreme Court in the case Nemi CA no. 8738/16 Sukhpal Singh & Anrs Vs. Delhi Admn /Food Inspector (PFA) Pages 19 of 15 Chand vs. State of Rajasthan II (2016) CCR 15 (SC). learned ASJ has rightly held it to be an offence punishable under Section 59(i) of FSSA Act for the purpose of awarding the punishment and no minimum sentence is prescribed for the above said offence. 5. Learned APP for the State fairly concedes that in the grounds of appeal there is no challenge to the finding of the learned ASJ that Dal Arhar coloured with synthetic colour "Tartrazine" is termed as "unsafe food" in terms of Sec.3(zz) (vii) of FSSA Act punishable under Section 59(i) of FSSA and no minimum sentence is prescribed there under. 6. Learned ASJ considered that since on the date of judgment and order on sentence in this case, the PFA Act, 1954 stood repealed, the learned Trial Court should have passed the order on sentence as per provisions of Food and Safety Standards Act, 2006 (FSSA) as held in Nemi Chand's case (supra). After placing reliance on the decision of the Supreme Court in Nemi Chand's case (supra), the learned ASJ arrived at the conclusion that adding colour to the food article i.e. Dal Arhar in the instant case, which was earlier punishable under Section 16(1A) of PFA Act has to be considered an offence punishable under Section 59(i) of FSSA, the sentence may extend to six months and also with fine which may extend to `1 lakh. 8. The case of the appellant is squarely covered by the decision of the CA no. 8738/16 Sukhpal Singh & Anrs Vs. Delhi Admn /Food Inspector (PFA) Pages 20 of 15 Supreme Court in Nemi Chand's case (supra).
